opening.spoken: This record covers the claimed solution of Erdős problem #550: what has been claimed, what it rests on, and what would have to be checked by whom.

short_version.spoken: Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp asked for an upper bound on the Ramsey number of a large tree against a complete multipartite graph in terms of the bipartite case. In June 2026 Eric Li posted a paper claiming the bound for every sufficiently large tree, and in August a Lean development. Nobody independent has reported building the development or reading the argument. Everything here is open.

what_happened.spoken: The claim was pinned from the public record: the problem page, the proof-claims thread, and every artifact the claimants made public, by commit or hash. Nothing was run. The gaps that follow are the checks still owed.

cycles.spoken: Eric Li posted the paper on arXiv; the Erdős-problems AI wiki listed it as a candidate full solution, marked unverified. The proof claim was listed on the problem page with links to the paper and a formalisation. The Lean repository was created and reached its current commit, and the paper's second version was posted, the same day. The problem page lists one proof claim, not marked accepted by the site; the repository has no licence file. A third-party formalisation of the problem statement exists.

background.spoken: Let T be a tree on n vertices with n large, and G the complete multipartite graph with class sizes m1 up to mk in increasing order. Show that the Ramsey number of T against G is at most the chromatic number of G minus one, times the Ramsey number of T against the complete bipartite graph on the two smallest classes minus one, plus m1. Chvátal's classical result gives the complete-graph case exactly.

background.spoken: The claim is the stated bound for every sufficiently large n and every n-vertex tree, with k minus one in place of the chromatic number minus one. The proof combines an off-Turán tree-embedding theorem, obtained from Szemerédi regularity and an embedding lemma of Hladký and Piguet, with a compactness-and-rounding theorem for bounded-rank hypergraph obstructions using shadow hypergraphs.
